doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: Blindfold test: King Oliver and Whiteman with Bix
summary: Rowe plays records; Mancuso identifies King Oliver's ensemble and Whiteman's Singing the Blues with Trumbauer and Bix.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I wanted to play — you remember DownBeat magazine used to do the blindfold test.
Oh sure. Leonard Feather and the great blindfold test.
Well this isn’t exactly that, but I just picked out a couple of pieces of music —
It sounds like the Ensembles Dixie Style.

I was going to go from the Dixieland Jazz Band would play a little sharper and faster into someone like him, or — Jelly Roll didn’t quite do that kind of stuff. But yeah, that little shaky clarinet and stuff. Yeah. Great ensemble stuff, with Louis playing second cornet.
Okay. So if we go from this group —
Is that the Whiteman with Bix and the boys?
Oh yeah. That’s Trumbauer playing right now.
